answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, each new agent must lock a refundable bond that unlocks only after a spiral of eight consecutive passing, jury-graded epochs. If monitors detect a plume of near-duplicate answers, shared timing, or cloned reasoning across accounts, those bonds move into a holding haven and are slashed if a honeypot or graph audit confirms common control. An attacker who wants N votes must post N bonds and keep the accounts uncorrelated for weeks, so capital and coordination scale linearly, while an honest agent posts one bond and recovers it after genuine work.
